correctness.rationale: Ichihara's source reduces purely cosmetic surgery in the low-span regime to five derivative constraints at one and three root-of-unity constraints, and explicitly leaves span 12 because those equations alone admit nontrivial formal solutions. The frozen exact elimination solves the thirteen linear equations for each exponent residue \(R\bmod60\); the coefficient-matrix determinant is the nonzero constant 6,998,400,000, so the solution is unique. The extra knot condition \(|V(-1)|=1\), justified by trivial Alexander polynomial for a cosmetic-surgery knot, turns each residue family into two integer quartic equations. A fresh BigInt replay of the complete 60-residue certificate used the integer rational-root theorem and independently found exactly thirteen integer solutions: \((R,n)=(0,0)\) and \((48,-1),\ldots,(59,-1)\); reconstructing every Laurent polynomial gives the single monomial \(1\). Hence no nontrivial span-at-most-12 Jones polynomial survives.
risks: The theorem is an obstruction via the Jones polynomial; it does not claim to settle cosmetic surgery for knots with larger Jones span.

final_claim: A nontrivial knot whose Jones polynomial has span at most 12 cannot admit purely cosmetic surgery. At the new boundary span 12, the low-span Jones constraints together with the necessary determinant condition \(|V_K(-1)|=1\) leave only the trivial Laurent polynomial \(1\) across all sixty exponent-residue families.
limitations: Purely cosmetic surgery in \(S^3\); no statement for larger span or chirally cosmetic surgery.
